findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Dynamic code execution sinks
 * @description Finds eval/exec/compile/import calls
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/dyn-code-sinks
 */
import python

from Call call
where
  call.getFunc().(Name).getId() in ["eval", "exec", "compile", "__import__", "execfile"]
select call, "dynamic code [" + call.getFunc().(Name).getId() + "]: " + call.toString()
findings.hypothesis: Dynamic code execution sinks (eval/exec/compile) exist in the debug console / debugger and may be reachable from HTTP requests.

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name File access with dynamic path
 * @description Finds open()/file reads where the path is not a literal
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/dynamic-file-open
 */
import python

from Call call
where
  call.getFunc().(Name).getId() in ["open"] and not call.getArg(0) instanceof Str
select call, "dynamic open: " + call.toString()
findings.hypothesis: File reads with dynamically computed paths (send_file, shared data, debugger tbtools) could allow path traversal / arbitrary file read.

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name form size limit attributes
 * @description Presence/absence of form parsing resource limits
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity note
 * @id py/form-limits
 */
import python

from Attribute a
where a.getName() in ["max_form_memory_size", "max_form_parts", "max_parts"]
select a, "limit attribute: " + a.getName()
findings.hypothesis: Werkzeug 2.2.2 multipart form parsing may lack a limit on the number of parts (max_form_parts was added in 3.0.1), leading to resource exhaustion (CWE-400).

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Presence of multipart limit identifiers
 * @description Checks which DoS-mitigation identifiers exist in the code base
 * @kind problem
 * @id py/multipart-limit-names
 * @problem.severity warning
 */
import python

from Name n
where n.getId() in ["max_form_parts", "num_bytes_dropped", "max_form_memory_size", "max_content_length"]
select n, "identifier present: " + n.getId()
findings.hypothesis: Werkzeug 2.2.2 lacks max_form_parts / num_bytes_dropped mitigations (CVE-2023-25577, CVE-2023-46136), while max_form_memory_size exists.

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name inspect shared_data and utils file handling
 * @description dump calls in SharedDataMiddleware and send_file regions
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity note
 * @id py/inspect-sinks-a
 */
import python

from Call c, string text
where
  c.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("%werkzeug/middleware/shared_data.py") and
  c.getLocation().getStartLine() >= 120 and c.getLocation().getStartLine() <= 180 and
  text = c.toString()
select c, "CALL: " + text
findings.hypothesis: SharedDataMiddleware may join untrusted URL path with the file root allowing traversal

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name safe_join internals
 * @description Dump calls used inside safe_join to audit path traversal protection
 * @kind problem
 * @id py/safe-join-internals
 * @problem.severity note
 */
import python

from Call c, Function f
where
  f.getName() = "safe_join" and
  c.getScope() = f
select c, "call in safe_join: " + c.getFunc().toString()

/**
 * @name cookie parser internals
 * @description list calls and string literals in sansio/http.py
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity note
 * @id py/cookie-internals
 */
import python

from Call c, string msg
where
  c.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath() = "src/werkzeug/sansio/http.py"
  and (
    exists(Name n | n = c.getFunc() and msg = "CALL: " + n.getId()) or
    msg = "OTHER"
  )
select c, msg
findings.hypothesis: Cookie parsing in sansio/http.py may allow malformed cookies (CWE-20), as in CVE-2023-23934.

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name __Host- cookie prefix handling
 * @description Checks whether any string literal references the __Host- cookie prefix
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/host-prefix-literal
 */
import python

from Str s
where s.getText().matches("%__Host%")
select s, "literal referencing __Host: " + s.getText()
findings.hypothesis: Werkzeug 2.2.2 parse_cookie lacks the __Host- prefix validation added in 2.2.3 (CVE-2023-23934): cookie names can be spoofed by placing them after another cookie, bypassing the __Host- security invariant.

message.text:
literal referencing __Host: Adjust the WSGI environ based on ``X-Forwarded-`` that proxies in
    front of the application may set.

    -   ``X-Forwarded-For`` sets ``REMOTE_ADDR``.
    -   ``X-Forwarded-Proto`` sets ``wsgi.url_scheme``.
    -   ``X-Forwarded-Host`` sets ``HTTP_HOST``, ``SERVER_NAME``, and
        ``SERVER_PORT``.
    -   ``X-Forwarded-Port`` sets ``HTTP_HOST`` and ``SERVER_PORT``.
    -   ``X-Forwarded-Prefix`` sets ``SCRIPT_NAME``.

    You must tell the middleware how many proxies set each header so it
    knows what values to trust. It is a security issue to trust values
    that came from the client rather than a proxy.

    The original values of the headers are stored in the WSGI
    environ as ``werkzeug.proxy_fix.orig``, a dict.

    :param app: The WSGI application to wrap.
    :param x_for: Number of values to trust for ``X-Forwarded-For``.
    :param x_proto: Number of values to trust for ``X-Forwarded-Proto``.
    :param x_host: Number of values to trust for ``X-Forwarded-Host``.
    :param x_port: Number of values to trust for ``X-Forwarded-Port``.
    :param x_prefix: Number of values to trust for
        ``X-Forwarded-Prefix``.

    .. code-block:: python

        from werkzeug.middleware.proxy_fix import ProxyFix
        # App is behind one proxy that sets the -For and -Host headers.
        app = ProxyFix(app, x_for=1, x_host=1)

    .. versionchanged:: 1.0
        Deprecated code has been removed:

        *   The ``num_proxies`` argument and attribute.
        *   The ``get_remote_addr`` method.
        *   The environ keys ``orig_remote_addr``,
            ``orig_wsgi_url_scheme``, and ``orig_http_host``.

    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
        All headers support multiple values. The ``num_proxies``
        argument is deprecated. Each header is configured with a
        separate number of trusted proxies.

    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
        Original WSGI environ values are stored in the
        ``werkzeug.proxy_fix.orig`` dict. ``orig_remote_addr``,
        ``orig_wsgi_url_scheme``, and ``orig_http_host`` are deprecated
        and will be removed in 1.0.

    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
        Support ``X-Forwarded-Port`` and ``X-Forwarded-Prefix``.

    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
        ``X-Forwarded-Host`` and ``X-Forwarded-Port`` modify
        ``SERVER_NAME`` and ``SERVER_PORT``.

literal referencing __Host: Return the host for the given parameters.

    This first checks the ``host_header``. If it's not present, then
    ``server`` is used. The host will only contain the port if it is
    different than the standard port for the protocol.

    Optionally, verify that the host is trusted using
    :func:`host_is_trusted` and raise a
    :exc:`~werkzeug.exceptions.SecurityError` if it is not.

    :param scheme: The protocol the request used, like ``"https"``.
    :param host_header: The ``Host`` header value.
    :param server: Address of the server. ``(host, port)``, or
        ``(path, None)`` for unix sockets.
    :param trusted_hosts: A list of trusted host names.

    :return: Host, with port if necessary.
    :raise ~werkzeug.exceptions.SecurityError: If the host is not
        trusted.

literal referencing __Host: Return the host for the given WSGI environment.

    The ``Host`` header is preferred, then ``SERVER_NAME`` if it's not
    set. The returned host will only contain the port if it is different
    than the standard port for the protocol.

    Optionally, verify that the host is trusted using
    :func:`host_is_trusted` and raise a
    :exc:`~werkzeug.exceptions.SecurityError` if it is not.

    :param environ: A WSGI environment dict.
    :param trusted_hosts: A list of trusted host names.

    :return: Host, with port if necessary.
    :raise ~werkzeug.exceptions.SecurityError: If the host is not
        trusted.

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name nameless cookie acceptance
 * @description parse_cookie accepts cookies with empty names that browsers may treat as __Host- prefixed
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/nameless-cookie
 */
import python

from If i, Compare cmp, Name n
where
  i.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath() in ["src/werkzeug/sansio/http.py", "src/werkzeug/http.py"] and
  cmp = i.getTest() and
  n = cmp.getAChildNode*() and
  n.getId() in ["key", "name", "k"]
select cmp, "cookie name check: " + cmp.toString()
findings.hypothesis: Cookie parser does not reject nameless cookies / __Host- prefix confusion (CVE-2023-23934)

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name cookie impl statements
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity note
 * @id py/cookie-impl
 */
import python

from Function f, Stmt s
where
  f.getName() in ["_cookie_parse_impl", "parse_cookie"] and
  s.getScope() = f and
  s.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("%werkzeug/sansio/http.py")
select s, f.getName() + " line " + s.getLocation().getStartLine().toString() + " :: " + s.toString()
findings.hypothesis: CVE-2023-23934: cookie parser accepts nameless cookies, bypassing __Host- prefix policy (CWE-20)

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name debugger host and pin validation identifiers
 * @description Lists identifiers used in the debug module related to host checking and pin auth
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/debug-host-identifiers
 */
import python

from Name n
where
  n.getId() in ["trusted_hosts", "is_debugger", "pin_auth", "_get_machine_id", "check_pin", "AnyHost", "_TrustedHosts"]
  and n.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("%debug%")
select n, "identifier: " + n.getId()
findings.hypothesis: Werkzeug debugger in 2.2.2 does not restrict which Host headers may access the interactive console, enabling RCE reachable via DNS rebinding / non-local host access (CVE-2024-34069).

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name multipart buffering before limit check
 * @description formparser multi-part loop accumulates chunks before enforcing limits
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/multipart-buffer
 */
import python

from Stmt s, Call c
where
  s.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath() = "src/werkzeug/formparser.py" and
  s.getLocation().getStartLine() >= 380 and s.getLocation().getStartLine() <= 430 and
  c.getLocation().getStartLine() >= 380 and c.getLocation().getStartLine() <= 430 and
  c = s.getAChildNode+()
select s, "STMT " + s.getLocation().getStartLine().toString() + " contains CALL " + c.getFunc().toString()
findings.hypothesis: Multipart form parsing buffers data without enforcing max_form_parts (CVE-2023-25577 / CVE-2023-46136 DoS)
